_strings.@@ef080a2087ef: Treaty conformity — ID conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from ID income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the ID return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Idaho's resident return (Form 40) starts on line 7 from federal adjusted gross income (federal Form 1040/1040-SR, line 11), and the only statutory additions are on Form 39R, Part A: (1) federal NOL deduction, (2) capital loss carryover incurred outside the state before becoming an Idaho resident, (3) non-Idaho state/local bond interest and dividends, (4) Idaho college savings account withdrawal, (5) bonus depreciation, (6) other additions. There is NO add-back of federally treaty-exempt income (unlike CA's Schedule CA). Because treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and is not added back, it flows through untaxed. Idaho also affirmatively confirms this in its Noncitizens guidance: 'Idaho honors all tax treaties recognized by the United States' and 'Gross income amounts exempt by treaty are not included in the gross income filing requirement for Idaho.' Therefore Idaho conforms to federal treaty exemptions.

state_tax.work_common_tail: . Tax line: Form 40, line 20: 'Tax from worksheet. See instructions, page 9.' Worksheet (instructions p.9): 1. 'Enter the amount of Idaho taxable income from Form 40, line 19'; 2. 'Enter the amount shown below for your filing status: Single or married filing separately, enter $4,489 — Married filing jointly, head of household, or qualifying surviving spouse, enter $8,978'; 3. 'Subtract line 2 from line 1. Enter the subtotal'; 4. 'Multiply subtotal by 5.8%'; 5. 'Idaho tax. Enter the total here and on Form 40, line 20.' Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): age_65 ($1,500 — NOT an exemption and NOT applied by calc.state_tax — it is an ADDITIONAL STANDARD DEDUCTION: $1,500 per age-65-or-older box checked on Form 40 line 12a ($1,850 instead if single or head of household), added to the base standard deduction via the Standard Deduction Worksheet, line 5 (instructions pp.8-9). Boxes must match the federal return.); blind ($1,500 — NOT an exemption and NOT applied by calc.state_tax — it is an ADDITIONAL STANDARD DEDUCTION: $1,500 per blind box checked on Form 40 line 12b ($1,850 instead if single or head of household), added to the base standard deduction via the Standard Deduction Worksheet, line 5 (instructions pp.8-9). Boxes must match the federal return.) This op computes the state's rate-schedule tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Base guidance: Supply Form 40, line 11 'Total Adjusted Income' = federal AGI (Form 40 line 7, from federal Form 1040/1040-SR line 11) plus Form 39R Part A additions minus Form 39R Part B subtractions. With no Idaho additions or subtractions this equals federal AGI. The op subtracts only the per-status standard deduction (Form 40 line 16); if you claim the federal qualified business income deduction (Form 40 line 18 = federal 1040 line 13) or itemize (Form 40 lines 13-15), the op will overstate tax — subtract your line 18 QBI amount from line 11 before supplying it, or compute on the form. Adjudication note (two-pass): base is federal_agi — Form 40 line 7 is federal adjusted gross income and Idaho taxable income derives from it via Idaho additions/subtractions and the deduction lines; supply the pre-standard-deduction figure as taxable_base (the op subtracts the federal-amount standard deduction; the line 18 QBI subtraction is the caller/form job — see notes). Idaho per-person amounts are CREDITS, so vector counts are zero by design. Structure: Idaho's 2023 tax is a single 5.8% rate on Idaho taxable income ABOVE a filing-status threshold — $4,489 (single or married filing separately) / $8,978 (married filing jointly, head of household, or qualifying surviving spouse) — per the Form 40 line 20 worksheet (2023 instructions p.9). It is modeled here as a 0% bracket up to the threshold and 5.8% above it; taxable income at or below the threshold owes $0. Head of household uses the SAME $8,978 worksheet threshold as married filing jointly (instructions p.9), even though its standard deduction ($20,800) differs from MFJ's ($27,700). Qualifying surviving spouse (Form 40 filing status 5) is listed in the worksheet with the same $8,978 amount as married filing jointly, so the engine's QSS-to-MFJ mapping is exact for both the brackets and the $27,700 standard deduction. 2023 rate change: the booklet's 'What's New for 2023' (p.1) states 'Tax Rate Reduction — Effective January 1, 2023, the individual income tax rate is 5.8%.' This flat 5.8% schedule is the FINAL one the 2023 filing season used, replacing Idaho's prior graduated schedule. Qualified business income deduction NOT modeled: Form 40 line 18 subtracts the federal QBI deduction (federal 1040/1040-SR line 13) AFTER the standard/itemized deduction to reach Idaho taxable income (line 19). See base_guidance for how to account for it. Itemizers NOT modeled: Form 40 lines 13-15 use federal Schedule A itemized deductions MINUS state and local income or general sales taxes (line 14 addback; capped per the federal $10,000/$5,000 SALT rule), and Idaho lets you ADD any federal foreign tax credit amount to Idaho itemized deductions; filers use the LARGER of net itemized (line 15) or the standard deduction (line 16). The op applies only the standard deduction. Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled (Standard Deduction Worksheet and 'You Must Itemize If', instructions pp.8-9): married filing separately MUST itemize if the spouse itemizes; dual-status nonresident aliens must itemize; a nonresident alien not from India gets a $0 standard deduction; a person claimable as another's dependent is limited to the greater of $1,250 or earned income + $400 (capped at the status amount); age-65+/blind boxes add $1,500 per box ($1,850 if single or head of household). Compute those cases on the worksheet. Idaho has NO personal or dependent exemptions. The per-person amounts on the return are TAX CREDITS subtracted from tax, not base reductions, and are not modeled: the Idaho Child Tax Credit is $205 per qualifying child age 16 or under (Form 40 line 25, nonrefundable), and the grocery credit is $120 per qualifying person ($140 if 65+) (Form 40 line 43, refundable). $10 Permanent Building Fund tax (Form 40 line 32) is a separate flat tax owed by everyone required to file an Idaho return (waived for those below the filing threshold, recipients of Idaho public assistance, and the legally blind). It is outside the line 20 computation and NOT modeled. No tax-table mandate: the 2023 booklet contains no tax tables — every filer computes line 20 with the worksheet, so bracket math reproduces the form exactly (whole-dollar rounding aside). The line 20 worksheet prints no explicit 'if less than zero, enter zero' step; the 0% floor bracket implements the $0 result for taxable income at or below the subtraction amount (the form provides no negative tax entry). Part-year residents and nonresidents file Form 43, not Form 40; Form 43 line 42 uses the identical worksheet (same $4,489/$8,978 amounts, same 5.8%) applied to Form 43 line 41 Idaho taxable income (instructions p.34). Form 40 face cross-check: 2023 Form 40 (EFO00089, 08-23-2023), https://tax.idaho.gov/wp-content/uploads/forms/EFO00089/EFO00089_08-23-2023.pdf — line 20 reads 'Tax from worksheet. See instructions, page 9', and the line-16 margin prints the standard deduction amounts ($13,850 single/MFS, $20,800 HOH, $27,700 MFJ/QSS).
